judgements.justification: A's AC wrote 'all reviewers were negative', which nMFp's unedited 6 contradicts, and omitted the rebuttal's BDD100K test and KITTI-MOTS results; the reject rests on that account.
Three of A's four reviewers never posted after the rebuttal and no A score moved, while B's reviewers replied and two raised to 7.
B's NPPQ said 'I am not an expert in MOTS' yet gave 7 at confidence 4, and B's AC counted it in the '7, 7, 6, 7' that carried acceptance.
A's ratings were 5, 6, 5, 5, not an even split, and B was unanimous above threshold.
Only A received the runtime comparison showing PCAN no faster than non-local attention, and B's speed table left out the faster STMask, so the committees saw different speed evidence.
B's NPPQ found no prior work, though Section 2 cites EM-based prototype attention [19], and that novelty reading fed B's scores.
B gave a spotlight with no rating above 7 and its meta-review states no reason for that tier.
h7Rc's objection rests on misreading YouTube-VIS as a VOS dataset, not on premises of a neighbouring field.
B's TiXB wrote the most careful review and stayed at 7 calling it 'a big step', while A's only positive reviewer, nMFp, gave four one-line strengths and never posted again.
No A reviewer or AC accepted the promised fixes and rejected for needing re-review; A's reject rests on scores and framing.
A's AC cites 'low novelty and insight' and an insufficient answer on self-supervised work that no public comment contains, and uses it to call all reviewers negative despite nMFp's 6.
A's h7Rc and AC faulted the paper as an application with no insight, while B valued the same method-and-benchmark contribution on its own terms.
x3ez's held 5 rests on the efficiency gain over non-local attention, which is central to the paper's claim, not peripheral.
